title: Why Do Birds Hit Windows? Up to 1 Billion a Year 🐦
description:
Why do birds fly straight into windows? Clear glass looks like open sky, and reflections of trees and clouds look like a real flight path, so birds crash into a wall they never see.

Sources:
https://abcbirds.org/?p=19069
https://www.audubon.org/news/window-strikes-are-even-deadlier-birds-we-thought
https://www.birdsavers.com/decalsdontwork/

Animated in the Whiteboard Explainer style.

topic: Why do birds fly straight into windows?
script:
Your window kills birds,
and they never see it coming. But why?
To a bird, your window is just more sky.
Clear glass lets a bird look straight through,
right at the plants inside.
Or the glass acts like a mirror,
showing trees and clouds behind it.
Either way, it sees an open path,
and flies full speed into a wall it never saw.
Nothing in nature is solid and see-through,
so birds never learned to expect it.
In the US,
scientists think windows kill up to a billion birds a year.
So what actually helps?
One hawk sticker barely helps.
The bird just flies around it.
But dots spaced about two inches apart
look like a fence,
so the bird turns away.
Next time you hear a thump,
go look at your window from outside.
What does a bird see in it?
key_facts: Birds perceive clear glass as open space and reflections of sky or vegetation as real habitat (American Bird Conservancy)
Collisions likely kill 365 million to about 1 billion birds a year in the US, median ~599 million (Loss et al. 2014 via ABC); newer studies suggest over 1 billion (Audubon 2024)
A single decal is just an obstacle to fly around; markings need gaps no larger than about 2 inches (ABC)
